name: Beef Wellington with Chestnut Stuffing & Roasted Cranberries
author: Rick Martinez
notes: A make-ahead project: the stuffing, broth reduction and wrapped beef can all be done the day before.

items: 4 ounces roasted chestnuts, smashed and chopped
2 large shallots, peeled and roughly chopped
1 1/2 pounds mixed mushrooms (such as shiitake, oyster, maitake, trumpet, and brown beech), roughly chopped
1 teaspoon sea salt, plus more for seasoning
1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, plus more for seasoning
1/4 cup beef tallow or unsalted butter
2 tablespoons beef tallow or extra-virgin olive oil
1 (3-pound) center cut beef tenderloin (also called Chateaubriand and center-cut filet mignon), trimmed
3 tablespoons sea salt, plus more for seasoning
2 tablespoons beef tallow or extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/2 pounds puff pastry (thawed if using frozen)
1 pound fresh cranberries (or thawed if using frozen)

method: For the mushroom stuffing: Add chestnuts, shallots, celery, and garlic to a food processor and pulse until finely chopped. Transfer to a large bowl. Add mushrooms to the food processor and pulse until mushrooms are pea-sized. Transfer to the bowl along with salt and pepper; stir to combine.

Melt beef tallow in a large heavy skillet, preferably cast iron, over medium-high heat. Add mushroom mixture, thyme, and bay leaves and stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid has evaporated and mushrooms are beginning to brown, 10 to 12 minutes. Season, remove bay leaves, and set aside to cool. Chill for at least 1 hour and up to 24 hours.

For bone broth reduction: Heat beef tallow in a large skillet over medium high and add shallots, garlic, thyme, bay leaves, and peppercorns and cook, tossing occasionally until just beginning to brown, about 4 minutes.

Remove from heat and carefully add bourbon, return to heat and tilt skillet toward flame to ignite. Cook until flames have died and almost all of the liquid has evaporated. Add bone broth and cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced by half, about 45 minutes. Strain, discard solids, and keep warm until ready to serve.
For the beef: Season the tenderloin with salt and pepper. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and chill for at least 1 hour and up to 24.

Once beef is chilled, heat beef tallow in a large skillet over high until very hot. Cook tenderloin, turning every 30 to 60 seconds, until all sides and the ends are browned, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a platter and brush all sides with Dijon mustard. Let rest for 30 minutes.

On a clean work surface, overlap long sheets of plastic wrap. Place crepes on top to make about a 14- by 7-inch rectangle, overlapping slightly so they are large enough to cover the tenderloin. Shingle bresaola over the crepes. Spread the chilled mushroom mixture over the bresaola in an even layer. Sprinkle apricots over top.

Place the beef along one long end and roll tightly around the tenderloin using the plastic to help you, peeling it back as you roll. Wrap the whole thing tightly in the plastic, twisting both ends like a candy wrapper. Chill for at least 30 minutes and up to overnight.

Heat oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a rimmed baking sheet with baking paper. Whisk the egg with 1 teaspoon water. Roll out about 450g of the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface to a 15- by 14-inch rectangle and lay it on baking paper. Brush egg over a rectangle about as wide as your piece of meat, leaving a 1-inch border.

Unwrap the beef log and place it along one long side of the pastry. Roll up tightly, then place seam-side down on the baking sheet. Tuck the pastry over the ends, pinching to seal and folding underneath. If adding a lattice, freeze for 10 to 15 minutes.

Lattice (optional): brush the pastry with egg, roll a lattice cutter across the remaining puff pastry and lay it over the top and sides. Press to adhere, brush with egg, and top with flaky salt and pepper. Freeze for another 10 to 15 minutes.

Bake until the pastry is golden brown all over and the meat is cooked to your liking (it will climb about 5°C while resting), about 40 to 50 minutes. If the pastry is already golden after 30 minutes, tent with foil. Rest on a wire rack for 20 minutes, leaving the oven on.

For the roasted cranberries: toss the cranberries with the sugar, wine, olive oil, rosemary, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Spread on a lined tray and bake at 220°C until bubbling, 20 to 30 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes.
Slice the Wellington into thick pieces. Serve with the broth reduction and roasted cranberries.

name: Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
author: Sasha Marx
notes: Broccoli rabe is sold as rapini or cime di rapa; broccolini works as a swap.

items: 3 tablespoons (45ml) extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
9 ounces (255g) sweet or hot Italian sausage (about 3 links), removed from casing
1 pound (450g; about 2 small bunches) broccoli rabe (rapini), ends trimmed, leaves picked and separated from stalks with florets
1 1/2 ounces (45g) finely grated Pecorino Romano, divided

method: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering. Pinch the sausage into small pieces into the pan in a single layer. Cook, undisturbed, until the bottom is light golden brown, about 2 minutes, then turn the pieces. Add garlic, anchovy (if using), and pepper flakes, and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds to 1 minute.

Increase heat to medium-high and add wine. Bring to a simmer and cook, swirling and scraping up any stuck-on bits, until the wine has emulsified with the oil and reduced slightly, about 30 seconds. Turn off heat.

Add the broccoli rabe stalks (with florets) to the boiling water and cook until barely tender, 1 1/2 to 2 minutes. Scoop out onto a plate. Add the leaves and cook about 1 minute, then scoop out, keeping the water boiling. Cut stalks and florets into 1 1/2-inch pieces and combine with the leaves.

Add orecchiette to the boiling water, stirring for the first 30 seconds. After 5 minutes, transfer 1 cup of pasta water to the skillet along with the broccoli rabe. Bring the skillet to a boil over high heat, swirling until the water emulsifies with the oil, 1 to 2 minutes.
Cook the pasta until about 3 minutes short of the packet time, then transfer it to the skillet (reserve at least 2 cups pasta water).
Cook on high, stirring and tossing, until the pasta is al dente and the sauce coats it, 2 to 3 minutes, adding more pasta water a little at a time. Keep it slightly looser than you want to serve it.
Remove from heat, stir in 3/4 of the cheese, and season with salt. Serve immediately with the remaining cheese.

name: Peking-Style Beef
author: Nicole Maguire
notes: The original has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 4.
method: Pour cooking oil into a hot skillet. Add the beef and break it up with a spatula. Cook until it starts caramelising on the edges.
Mix hoisin sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar and a pinch of Chinese five-spice in a bowl.
Add the garlic to the beef and stir, then pour over the sauce and mix until the meat is coated.
Stir in a cornflour slurry and keep stirring until glossy.
Serve over white rice with cucumber ribbons, garnished with spring onions, a drizzle of sesame oil and sesame seeds.

name: Oven-Baked Doner Kebab
author: Yumna | Feel Good Foodie
notes: The original has no quantities; amounts are a guide for 4.
method: Place the beef in a bowl. Grate in the onion, press in the garlic, and add a few spoons of Greek yoghurt and the spices.
Mix well by hand, then spread the mixture onto baking paper and roll into a tight log.
Put the log on a baking tray with sliced red onions and tomato wedges and bake at 200°C for about 35-40 minutes until cooked through.
Slice the meat thinly and serve in pita bread with the onions, tomatoes, pickled peppers and white garlic sauce (or yoghurt mixed with garlic).

name: Slow-Roasted Crispy Pork Belly
author: Nagi
notes: Dry the skin in the fridge overnight if you can. Don't score the skin.

items: 1kg / 2 lb pork belly with skin on, NOT SCORED. Look for 3 – 3.5cm / 1.2 – 1.6" thick, even thickness with flat, unwrinkled skin, preferably not vac-packed (Note 1)
1/2 tsp fennel powder / ground fennel seeds, optional, Note 3
1 tsp salt, cooking/kosher salt (or 7/8 tsp table salt), divided
See in post for more Sauce options

method: Dry skin overnight: Place pork belly on a plate. Pat skin dry with paper towels. Leave uncovered in fridge overnight to dry out the skin. (If you don't have time, pat the skin dry as best you can).
Preheat oven to 140°C/285°F (120°C fan).
Season flesh: Drizzle flesh (only) with 1 tsp oil. Sprinkle over 1/2 tsp salt, the pepper and fennel powder. Rub all over the flesh, including on the sides.

Wrap in foil: Place 2 pieces of foil on a work surface. Put the belly in middle of foil, skin side up. Fold the sides in to enclose the belly, forming an open box, pinching corners to seal tightly and make it as snug as possible. Place meat on a tray.
Season skin: Pat skin dry with paper towels. Rub with 1/2 tsp oil then sprinkle remaining 1/2 tsp salt evenly all over the skin surface.
Slow roast 2 1/2 hours: Roast for 2 1/2 hours. After 1 1/2 hours, remove and tighten the foil (pork will have shrunk), and continue cooking.
Increase heat: Remove pork from oven, then increase heat to 240°C/465°F (all oven types).
Level pork: Remove pork from foil and place on a rack set over a tray. Use scrunched up balls of foil under the pork so the skin is as level as possible.
30 minutes on high heat: Roast for 30 minutes, rotating after 15 minutes as needed, until the crackling is deep golden, puffy and crispy all over. Protect any patches browning too fast with foil.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice into 2cm thick slices with a serrated knife. Serve with apple sauce.

name: Pork and Spring Onion Dumplings with Crispy Skirt
author: Sohla El-Waylly
notes: Makes 24. The original method wasn't saved; these steps are a guide.

items: ½ tsp. freshly ground white or black pepper

method: Finely chop the spring onions and grate the ginger. Mix with the pork, 2 tsp soy sauce, 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper.
Place a heaped teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, wet the edge and fold into a half-moon, pleating to seal.
Whisk 1 cup water with 2 tbsp rice vinegar, the flour, cornflour and a pinch of salt to make the slurry.

Heat a little oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high. Arrange the dumplings flat-side down, pour in enough slurry to come a few millimetres up the sides, cover and cook until the water evaporates and a lacy golden crust forms, about 8 minutes.
Invert onto a plate, crust side up. Mix the remaining soy sauce and vinegar (and chilli oil) for dipping.

name: Easy Beef Taco Bowls
author: Rachel Gurjar
notes: The original method wasn't saved; these steps are a guide.

items: ¼ medium red onion, finely chopped
1 jalapeño, ½ finely chopped, ½ coarsely chopped
Cooked rice, sliced avocado, tortilla chips, shredded lettuce, and lime wedges (for serving)

method: Make a quick salsa: mix the tomato, red onion, finely chopped jalapeño, coriander, 2 tbsp lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Blitz the brown onion, garlic and coarsely chopped jalapeño to a paste (or chop very finely).
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high, add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned and crisp in places.
Add the onion paste and cook until the liquid evaporates, then stir in the taco seasoning with a splash of water and the remaining lime juice.
Serve over rice with the salsa, avocado, lettuce, corn chips and lime wedges.

name: Smash Burger Tacos
author: Madeleine Storace
notes: Amounts are per person: scale up for the household.
method: Press 50 grams of beef mince into each corn tortilla.
Season with taco seasoning.
Place tortillas face down on a pan and cook until crispy.
Flip and add cheese, allowing it to melt.
For the sauce, mix Greek yogurt with sriracha, taco seasoning, and tomato sauce.
Top cooked tortillas with sauce, lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickles.

name: Turkey Burgers
author: Martha Rose Shulman
notes: The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide.

items: 1 tablespoon canola oil, or use pan spray

method: Grate half the onion and mix gently with the turkey, Worcestershire sauce, ketchup, salt and pepper. Shape into 4 patties.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan or on a grill over medium-high and cook the patties for about 5 minutes a side until cooked through.
Toast the buns and build the burgers with sliced tomato, onion, lettuce, pickles, red capsicum, ketchup and mustard.

name: Restaurant-Quality Beef Massaman Curry
author: Jasmin's Eats
notes: Uses Maesri massaman curry paste (yellow can). Slow cook for about 4 hours until the beef falls apart.

items: 3/4 puck of palm sugar (or 1-2 tbsp brown sugar depending how sweet you like it)

method: Cut the beef into large chunks and sear in the olive oil until browned all over. Set aside.
Cook the curry paste with half a can of coconut cream for 5-10 minutes, until the oil separates and rises to the top.
Add the beef, onions, potatoes, carrots, the rest of the coconut cream and the water. Season with palm sugar, fish sauce and tamarind.
Slow cook for about 4 hours, or until everything is fork tender and the meat falls apart. Taste and adjust the salty, sour and sweet to your liking.
Serve with rice, topped with herbs and chopped salted peanuts.
